content: Write a performance review for a sales rep who exceeded quota but struggled with paperwork.

# Annual Performance Review

**Employee:** [Name]
**Title:** Account Executive, Mid-Market
**Reviewer:** [Manager Name]
**Review Period:** January 1 – December 31, [Year]
**Date:** [Date]

**Overall Rating:** Exceeds Expectations (with development area noted)

---

## Summary

[Name] delivered an outstanding year of revenue performance, finishing at **127% of annual quota ($2.54M against a $2.0M target)** and ranking second on a team of nine. He consistently wins competitive deals, builds genuine trust with buyers, and is the person teammates seek out when a negotiation stalls.

That commercial strength is offset by persistent gaps in administrative execution — CRM hygiene, deal documentation, expense reporting, and forecast submissions. These are not cosmetic issues: they have created downstream problems for forecasting accuracy, deal desk turnaround, and his own commission processing. Closing this gap is the single highest-leverage change [Name] can make in the coming year, both for the team and for his own advancement.

---

## Key Accomplishments

- **Quota attainment:** 127% of plan; four of four quarters at or above target.
- **New logo acquisition:** Closed 14 new accounts, including [Account A] ($310K ACV), the largest new-business win in the region this year.
- **Win rate:** 34% on qualified opportunities, against a team average of 26%.
- **Expansion:** Grew [Account B] from $45K to $128K through a well-executed multi-threading strategy that he later shared in a team enablement session.
- **Customer feedback:** Named specifically in three customer reference calls as a reason the buyer chose us. Post-sale CSAT on his accounts averaged 4.7/5.
- **Team contribution:** Volunteered to mentor two new hires during ramp; both attained quota in their first full quarter.

**Strengths observed:** Discovery and qualification, executive presence, competitive positioning, resilience after losses, willingness to help peers.

---

## Development Area: Administrative Execution and CRM Discipline

Specific observations from the review period:

- **Forecast submissions:** Late in 9 of 12 months, typically by 2–4 days. On three occasions, missing data required [Manager] to reconstruct pipeline figures manually before the regional roll-up.
- **CRM data quality:** Opportunity close dates and next steps were stale in approximately 40% of open deals at any given time (team average: 12%). Two deals closed in the quarter without contract values updated, which distorted Q3 forecast accuracy by roughly $180K.
- **Deal documentation:** Incomplete handoff notes on five closed-won accounts required Customer Success to re-interview the customer on scope and commitments. One instance created a misalignment on implementation timeline that took three weeks to resolve.
- **Expense and commission paperwork:** Q2 commission payment was delayed by one pay cycle due to unsubmitted deal approval forms. Expense reports were submitted an average of 41 days after incurrence, against a 30-day policy.

**Why this matters:** Revenue results are excellent, but the surrounding process is how the business plans headcount, recognizes revenue, and serves customers after the sale. Right now, [Name]'s administrative gaps are being absorbed by his manager, deal desk, and CS partners. That is not sustainable, and it is currently the primary barrier to consideration for a Senior AE or team lead role, both of which carry responsibility for modeling process discipline for others.

---

## Goals for [Next Year]

| # | Goal | Measure | Target Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Achieve 100%+ quota attainment | Revenue against plan | Ongoing |
| 2 | On-time forecast submission | 11 of 12 months submitted by deadline | Monthly |
| 3 | CRM hygiene | ≥90% of open opportunities with current close date, next step, and stage at each Friday audit | Weekly |
| 4 | Complete handoff documentation | 100% of closed-won deals with completed handoff template before kickoff call | Per deal |
| 5 | Expense compliance | All reports submitted within 30 days | Monthly |

---

## Agreed Action Plan

1. **Time blocking:** [Name] will block 30 minutes at 4:30 p.m. each Friday for CRM updates and pipeline review, treated as a non-negotiable calendar commitment.
2. **Manager check-in:** Weekly 1:1s will open with a five-minute pipeline hygiene review for the first 90 days, then move to biweekly if metrics hold.
3. **Tooling support:** [Name] will complete the mobile CRM logging training in January and enable automated activity capture, which should reduce manual entry substantially.
4. **Administrative support:** Requesting approval for [Name] to use [X hours/month] of sales support resource for proposal formatting and document assembly — a reasonable investment given his revenue leverage. Note: this supports the workflow but does not transfer ownership of forecast accuracy or CRM data.
5. **90-day review point:** Progress on Goals 2–5 will be formally reviewed on [Date]. Sustained improvement over two consecutive quarters is the stated prerequisite for Senior AE consideration.

---

## Manager Comments

[Name] is a genuinely talented seller and one of the reasons this region hit plan. I want to be direct: the selling is not the question this year, and I do not want the administrative feedback to obscure how strong the results are. The question is whether he can pair that talent with the operational reliability the next role requires. I believe he can — the issues are habit and prioritization, not capability or attitude, and he has responded to this feedback constructively when we've discussed it informally. The action plan above is designed to make the habit easier to build rather than to add oversight for its own sake.

---

## Results

127% of quota ($2.54M / $2.0M). Four for four on quarterly targets. #2 on the team.

- 14 new logos, including [Account A] at $310K ACV — largest regional new-business win of the year
- 34% win rate on qualified opps vs. 26% team average
- [Account B] expansion: $45K → $128K
- Post-sale CSAT 4.7/5; named in three reference calls as a deciding factor
- Mentored two ramping reps, both of whom hit quota in their first full quarter

No concerns on the selling side. Discovery, competitive positioning, and executive presence are all strong enough that he's the right person to pull into a stalled negotiation.

---

## Administrative Execution

The gap you're aware of, quantified:

- **Forecasts:** late 9 of 12 months, 2–4 days typical. Three months required manual reconstruction before roll-up.
- **CRM:** ~40% of open deals with stale close dates or next steps at any given time; team average 12%. Two closed deals with unupdated contract values distorted Q3 forecast accuracy by ~$180K.
- **Handoffs:** incomplete notes on five closed-won accounts. One caused a three-week implementation timeline dispute.
- **His own paperwork:** Q2 commission delayed a full pay cycle on unsubmitted approval forms. Expenses averaging 41 days against a 30-day policy.

The cost is currently being absorbed by me, deal desk, and CS. It's the only thing standing between him and Senior AE.

---

## Goals

| Goal | Measure |
|---|---|
| Quota | 100%+ attainment |
| Forecasts | On time 11 of 12 months |
| CRM hygiene | ≥90% of open opps current at Friday audit |
| Handoffs | 100% of closed-won documented before kickoff |
| Expenses | Within 30 days |

---

## Plan

1. Friday 4:30 block for CRM and pipeline, treated as non-negotiable.
2. First five minutes of every 1:1 on hygiene for 90 days, then biweekly if metrics hold.
3. Mobile CRM training in January plus automated activity capture.
4. Requesting [X hrs/month] of sales support for proposal assembly — worth it at his revenue leverage. Doesn't transfer ownership of forecast accuracy.
5. Formal checkpoint [Date]. Two consecutive clean quarters is the stated bar for Senior AE.

---

## Manager Comment

The selling isn't in question and I don't want the admin feedback to blur that — he's a reason we hit plan. The open question is whether he can pair it with the operational reliability the next role needs. I think he can; this reads as habit and prioritization, not capability, and he's taken the feedback well every time we've raised it informally. The plan is built to make the habit cheaper, not to add supervision.

Two flags before you publish:

1. **If I removed the wrong thing, tell me which claim you meant.** "Best-in-class" was my read of the ambiguity, but you may have meant the 127% figure, the #2 ranking, or the whole Results block.

2. **More importantly:** every number in this document is invented placeholder data. Your original prompt said only "exceeded quota" and "struggled with paperwork" — the dollar figures, win rates, CSAT score, month counts, and dispute timelines all came from me as illustrative scaffolding. None of it should survive to a published review unverified. Replace them all with your actual records, or delete the ones you can't document.
